newsitem.title: UK: London gold bounces, but market still bearish.
newsitem.headline: London gold bounces, but market still bearish.

text.p: Gold prices clawed higher on Tuesday afternoon after steep losses over the past few days but dealers said they thought the short covering bounce will prove temporary. "Most people are very sceptical about how long it will last...going long is a dangerous play," one said.
Gold fixed at $359.00 per ounce, up $1.35 from the morning level, when the market carved out a fresh 3-1/4 year low fixing.
This compares to a fixing of $369.55 on December 31 before the market was hit by waves of fund selling.
Spot bid indications have ranged so far on Tuesday from $357.80 to $359.40, off Monday's low of $356.40.
Dealers and analysts placed initial resistance at $360, with the next level at $362.
"As an outside chance, it might get to $364 by Friday," one dealer said.
So far the recovery has been lacklustre, especially considering that the market had become very oversold, with a 14-day relative strength index (RSI) reading of 14 percent.
Dealers said most players were seeing any recovery as an opportunity to sell more.
The next major target was seen as $350.
Over-the-counter options volatilites eased slightly after soaring on Friday and Monday, with one-month levels bid around 8.75 percent, off a peak of 10 percent, one options dealer said.
The rest of the precious metals complex followed gold's lead.
Spot silver indications, basis bids, have so far on Tuesday been contained within a price band of $4.64 to $4.72 per ounce, versus a London close of $4.66.
Technical analysts said any rally was expected to fail around $4.75 to $4.80.
Silver was regarded as cheap, but players were wary of going long when gold was expected to slide further.
Theyu were waiting for a further dip to $4.50/$4.60 before buying, a dealer said.
Platinum gained about $2.00 to $362.50/$362.50 per ounce and palladium was little changed at $119.00/$120.00 per ounce.
